column2: In the same pan, sauté the onion and garlic for 3 minutes, then the vegetables for 5–6 minutes.
Add the tomato paste and herbs, return the chicken and add 2–3 spoons of water.
Cook covered for 8–10 minutes until the thickest part of the chicken reaches 74 °C and is no longer pink.
Sear the chicken without crowding so it doesn’t release water and stew.
You can vary the flavour with mustard, lemon or ginger.
Serve hot with rice or bulgur pilaf.
Baked lemon and herb fish
4 portions fish (sea bass, sea bream, salmon, trout or whiting; fillet or whole)
2 lemons
Half a bunch dill or 1 dessert spoon thyme
2 tomatoes (optional)
Preheat the oven to 200 °C and line a tray with baking paper.
Score diagonal cuts on both sides of a whole fish; pat fillets dry with paper towels.
Make a sauce with olive oil, lemon juice, crushed garlic, herbs, salt and pepper and brush it over the fish.
Place the fish on the tray and arrange lemon and tomato slices around it.
Bake fillets for 12–15 minutes and whole fish for 20–25, until the flesh is opaque and comes easily off the bones.
Oily fish (salmon, mackerel) go well with mustard and dill; white fish with lemon and thyme.
Serve hot with rocket salad and lemon.
Vegetable pasta in olive oil
350 g pasta
2 cups chopped vegetables (zucchini, mushroom, tomato, eggplant, peas or cauliflower)
Grated zest of 1 lemon (optional)
Half a cup grated cheese
A handful of fresh herbs (basil, mint, thyme or dill)
Boil the pasta in plenty of salted water and reserve 1 cup of the water.
Stir the garlic in olive oil for 1 minute.
Add the vegetables and sauté over high heat for 6–8 minutes.
Add the pasta, lemon zest and a little cooking water and mix for 1 minute.
Serve with cheese and fresh herbs.
Cooking water binds the sauce; add it little by little.
Yogurt cup with fruit and nuts
500 g strained yogurt
1.5 cups fruit or cooked pumpkin (apple, pear, strawberry, peach, apricot, fig or date)
4 tablespoons nuts (walnuts, almonds or hazelnuts)
2 tablespoons honey or grape molasses
2 tablespoons tahini (optional)
Dice the fruit small; soften apple and pear in a pan with cinnamon for 5 minutes and let cool.
Toast the nuts in a dry pan for 2 minutes and chop coarsely.
Whisk the yogurt with the honey.
Layer the yogurt, fruit and nuts in glasses.
Drizzle with tahini and chill for 30 minutes.
Dates and figs are sweet, so you can reduce the honey.
1 day in the fridge.
Vegetable yogurt dip
500 g vegetables (beetroot, zucchini, carrot, broccoli, cauliflower, chard or eggplant)
2 tablespoons walnuts or 2 tablespoons tahini
Prepare the vegetable: boil and grate beetroot, grate and sauté zucchini and carrot, boil broccoli and cauliflower, roast eggplant.
Let the vegetable cool and chop finely or mash.
Mix the vegetable with the walnuts or tahini.
Don’t mix with the yogurt until the vegetable has cooled completely.
Cold, with bread or lavash.
Baked garlic zucchini
2 medium zucchini
A little salt
Wash the zucchini and cut into 1 cm half-moons; blot excess moisture with paper towels.
Crush the garlic and mix with olive oil, thyme and a little salt; coat the vegetables with this sauce.
Spread the vegetables in a single layer on a tray lined with baking paper; place in an oven preheated to 200°C.
Bake for 20–30 minutes until soft and golden at the edges; turn halfway through.
Baked garlic eggplant
2 medium eggplants
Peel the eggplants in stripes and dice; soak in salted water for 15 minutes and pat dry well.
Baked garlic cauliflower
Separate the cauliflower into small florets and wash; halve any very large pieces.
Baked garlic broccoli
1 medium broccoli
Separate the broccoli into florets, slice the thick stems thinly and dry well.
Baked garlic leeks
3 leeks
Cut the leeks lengthwise, wash the layers well and cut into 3 cm pieces.
Bake for 30–35 minutes until the vegetables are completely soft and golden at the edges; cover briefly if needed.
Baked garlic spinach
350 g spinach
Wash the spinach in plenty of water, drain, separate the thick stems and chop coarsely.
Mix the garlic with olive oil; put the leaves and stems in a wide baking dish.
Bake the tough stems first at 190°C for 8 minutes; add the leaves and stir.
Bake for another 8–12 minutes until the leaves wilt and soften; serve with lemon.
Baked garlic chard
Wash and dry the chard leaves; slice the tough stems thinly and the leaves coarsely.
Baked garlic celeriac
1 medium celeriac
Peel the celeriac and cut into 2 cm cubes; keep in lemon water so it doesn’t brown.
Baked garlic carrots
4 medium carrots
Peel the carrots and cut into sticks of even thickness, about 1 cm.
Baked garlic mushrooms
Clean the mushrooms with a damp cloth and halve them; don’t soak them in water.
Toss the garlic, olive oil and thyme with the mushrooms.
Spread the mushrooms in a single layer on a wide tray; bake at 200°C for 15 minutes.
Once they release their liquid and brown at the edges, stir; bake 5–8 more minutes and serve.
Yogurt vegetable salad (borani style)
500 g vegetables (zucchini, eggplant, spinach, chard, leek, carrot or cauliflower)
2 cups strained yogurt
2 cloves garlic (crushed)
4–5 sprigs dill
Prepare the vegetable: grate zucchini and carrot, finely chop spinach/chard/leek, roast and chop eggplant, separate cauliflower into small florets and boil.
Sauté the vegetable in half the olive oil for 6–8 minutes until the liquid evaporates; add salt and let cool completely.
Whisk the yogurt with the garlic and dill.
Mix the cooled vegetable with the yogurt and transfer to a serving plate.
Heat the remaining olive oil, add the chilli flakes and drizzle over the salad.
If the vegetables are added to the yogurt while hot, the yogurt curdles and turns watery.
Serve cold; it goes well with meat and chicken dishes.
Keeps for 2 days in a closed container in the fridge.
Vegetable and cheese omelette
4 eggs
1 cup finely chopped vegetables (zucchini, spinach, chard, mushroom, leek or broccoli)
Half a cup grated kashar or crumbled white cheese
A pinch of black pepper
4–5 sprigs parsley
Finely chop the vegetables; separate broccoli and cauliflower into small florets and boil for 3 minutes.
Melt the butter in a pan, add the vegetables and sauté for 4–5 minutes until the liquid evaporates.
Whisk the eggs with the milk, salt and pepper until frothy.
Pour the mixture over the vegetables; when the edges set over low heat, push them towards the centre with a spatula.
While the top is still slightly runny, sprinkle with the cheese, cover and cook for 2 minutes.
Fold the omelette in half and serve with parsley.
Sauté watery vegetables (zucchini, spinach) first to drive off the liquid so the omelette doesn’t go soggy.
If using white cheese, reduce the salt.
Serve hot with tomato, cucumber and toasted bread.
Eat fresh; don’t leave it standing.
